title: Governed restart for completed but inactive Hostinger Production build

phases.objective: Provide one owner-authorized exact-main-head and exact-Production-SHA Hostinger Node.js restart with trusted bot-only claim history, an outer workflow revalidation, an in-process authority gate inside the exact provider-call path, a durable local attempt journal written only after that gate passes and before network dispatch, fail-closed missing-report semantics, and coherent top-level Production runtime identity proof.

e2e_journeys.actor: repository owner and trusted default-branch GitHub Actions runner
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Owner workflow_dispatch carrying the exact current main SHA and completed Hostinger build UUID, or the equivalent exact owner-authored Issue #4953 trigger
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The workflow fails closed if authorization, repository state, Production, incident state, completed build, trusted marker authority, claim ownership, in-process pre-mutation authority, provider-attempt durability, secret availability, or coherent runtime identity differs. The exact Issue, main SHA, Production SHA, binding, run ID, and latest trusted claim are re-read inside the provider-call path after Hostinger prechecks and immediately before attempt journaling and POST dispatch. Failures proven to occur before provider dispatch can release the same run claim. A durable attempt journal, ambiguous provider response, missing report after dispatch, or confirmed restart consumes or leaves unresolved the exact binding and cannot be retried automatically. Success requires deployment-info itself to report the exact Production branch and SHA through direct top-level fields.
steps: Receive explicit owner workflow_dispatch inputs or the equivalent exact owner trigger on open Issue #4953.
Resolve and validate the full expected_head_sha and exact expected_build_uuid before any write.
Reject main and Production as repository mutation targets; only Issue metadata and the existing Hostinger runtime process are eligible for mutation.
Verify current main equals the authorized full SHA, protected Production equals f5c1ae8840b4d4452f2908bb0f23051880bb6896, and Issue #4953 remains open.
Read every paginated Incident marker but trust exact-once state only when authored by github-actions[bot].
Reject completed, provider-attempted, provider-performed, or unresolved trusted claims for the exact Production-SHA and build-UUID binding.
Create a trusted status=claiming marker bound to the current run and expose claimed=true only after GitHub accepts it.
Checkout the explicitly authorized main SHA and execute the restart implementation regression contract.
Run a workflow-level defense-in-depth revalidation of main, Production, Issue state, expected_head_sha, and trusted claim ownership before starting provider prechecks.
Fetch Hostinger build history and require the exact completed post-merge build 019fc51c-3947-7255-aa4d-f55cb8df7658 with Git source.
Read health, version, and deployment-info before mutation and skip restart only when deployment-info itself contains the exact Production branch and SHA pair in direct top-level fields.

Inside the exact Hostinger POST fetch path, re-read Issue #4953, main, Production, and all paginated trusted binding markers; require the current run claim to match expected_head_sha, be the latest claim, and have no later marker.
If the in-process authority gate fails, record restart_attempted=false, send no provider POST, create no attempt journal, and publish a same-run retryable non-mutating final marker.
After the in-process authority gate passes, write hostinger-nodejs-production-restart-attempt.json with restart_attempted=true, provider_mutation_attempted=true, and pre_mutation_authority=passed.
If the provider response is lost or the final report is missing after the attempt journal exists, consume or leave unresolved the binding and prohibit automatic retry.
If execution stops before the attempt journal exists, publish a same-run trusted retryable release proving restart_attempted=false and provider_mutation_attempted=false.
Poll bounded public runtime endpoints and require exact coherent Production identity from deployment-info without cross-endpoint, nested-object, or MIME-header bypass.
Upload structured secret-free evidence including runtime identity and pre-mutation authority reports, then publish a bounded trusted marker while keeping Incident #4953 open.
assertions: The production workflow has workflow_dispatch and issue_comment entrypoints but no push, pull_request, or pull_request_target production trigger.
Only the repository owner workflow dispatch or exact owner Issue #4953 trigger can enter the restart job.
The workflow grants contents:read and issues:write only and cannot mutate repository contents or protected refs.
Only github-actions[bot] markers participate in consumed, unresolved, or retryable exact-once calculations.
An untrusted public Issue comment cannot consume, release, or supersede a restart claim.
Main, Production, and Incident state are verified before the claim, at the workflow-level pre-provider checkpoint, and again inside the exact provider-call path.

The in-process authority report uses contract mad4b.hostinger-pre-mutation-authority.v1 and proves Issue open, exact main and Production SHAs, exact binding and run ID, latest claim ownership, and zero later markers.
The current run must own the latest trusted unresolved claim at both pre-provider revalidation points.
The in-process authority callback completes before persistAttemptJournal(configuration), mutationState.attempted=true, and the Hostinger fetch call.
A failed in-process authority check sends zero provider POSTs, leaves restart_attempted=false, and creates no attempt journal.
A durable attempt journal is written synchronously after passed in-process authority and before the Hostinger POST is dispatched.
A missing or invalid report with an attempt journal cannot produce restart_attempted=false or retryable_without_provider_mutation=true.
A pre-provider failure without an attempt journal may release only the same run claim as restart_attempted=false and provider_mutation_attempted=false.
status=completed, restart_attempted=true, or restart_performed=true consumes the exact binding.
An ambiguous POST transport result is classified restart_attempted_outcome_unconfirmed and cannot be retried automatically.
The implementation rejects newer, different, or non-completed builds before provider mutation.
The only Hostinger provider mutation is the official Node.js server restart endpoint.
Version observations cannot supply a missing SHA or branch to deployment-info.
Nested historical objects cannot supply a missing SHA or branch.
JSON identity suppression is applied after successful JSON parsing regardless of application/json, application/*+json, text/plain, or missing MIME metadata.

Success after a provider attempt requires both a passed in-process authority report and deployment-info exposing Production and f5c1ae8840b4d4452f2908bb0f23051880bb6896 through accepted direct top-level fields in the same response.
The operation never creates a build, uploads an archive, redeploys, changes branch binding, runs SQL, applies migrations, mutates a database, or outputs secrets.

phases.objective: Merge the exact-head governed implementation, authorize one current-main-bound restart, and attach its attempt journal, in-process authority report, runtime report, artifact digest, and trusted marker to Incident #4953.

Exercise stale head before claim and during Hostinger prechecks, changed Production, closed Incident, newer build, duplicate trigger, untrusted marker spoofing, missing or superseded current-run claim, a later trusted marker, missing secret, provider rejection, ambiguous POST transport, missing report before and after journal creation, split endpoint identity, cross-object identity, non-standard JSON MIME, and post-restart stale runtime while remaining fail-closed.
The operation restarts the existing Production Node.js process and does not create a separate canary deployment.
Record exact in-process GitHub authority and coherent top-level Production runtime parity after the one-time restart, retaining fail-closed evidence when authority or runtime parity fails.
